change: Primary corrected: removed Gluteus Medius from primary. The glute kickback is a hip extension exercise where Gluteus Maximus is the clear prime mover. Gluteus Medius acts as a stabilizer (hip abduction/rotation) and belongs in secondary. Moved Gluteus Medius to its own secondary entry. All other secondary muscles (Hamstrings, Lower Back, abs) confirmed correct.

No changes. Primary (glutes both heads + full quads) and secondary (Adductors, Hamstrings, Calves, abs) confirmed correct. EMG and biomechanics research confirms curtsy lunge is particularly effective for Gluteus Medius. Adductors secondary confirmed due to crossover step pattern.

No changes. Primary (Quads, glutes both heads, Adductors) and secondary (Hamstrings, Calves, abs) confirmed correct. Lateral lunge research confirms Adductors as a co-primary target alongside Quads and Glutes. EMG data supports high adductor and gluteus medius activation.

Secondary corrected: removed Gluteus Medius from the glutes secondary entry; kept only Gluteus Maximus. The landmine hack squat is a knee-dominant quad exercise — Gluteus Maximus assists with hip extension at the top, but Gluteus Medius (abductor/stabilizer) is not a meaningful secondary mover in this bilateral squat pattern. All other secondary muscles (Hamstrings, Calves, Lower Back) confirmed correct.

No changes. Primary (Anterior Deltoids) confirmed — anterior delt is dominant in landmine press due to shoulder flexion arc. Secondary (Triceps, upper chest Clavicular Head, abs, obliques) all confirmed. Lateral Deltoids not added as primary since the arc of the landmine press is predominantly shoulder flexion (anterior delt), not abduction. Obliques confirmed essential for anti-rotation in the unilateral half-kneeling position.
